narrative:
The model predicts you have a 37% chance of failing your final year, which is high enough that the school requires you to take remedial courses to strengthen your performance before moving forward.

The prediction is driven mainly by three key aspects of your situation. By far the strongest factor is your history of three past class failures. While students who passed had zero previous failures on average, your repeated setbacks sent a strong signal that you are at much higher risk this year.

Two other factors pulled the prediction in the opposite direction, toward passing. The fact that you did not attend nursery school worked in your favor, as did your relatively low amount of free time after school. Both of these characteristics are more commonly seen among students who ultimately succeed.

Even though these positive elements helped reduce the risk, they were not enough to overcome the heavy influence of your past academic struggles. To improve your chances, you should focus on breaking the pattern of failure by creating a consistent daily study routine, seeking extra academic support early, and speaking with your teachers about targeted help in the subjects that have been hardest for you. Small, steady improvements now can still change the outcome.
